finding: The red exact-semantic-merge regression is causally explained by an internal validator contract mismatch, not by embedding similarity or nondeterministic behavior. _merge_exact_equivalents can validly collapse two formally equivalent branches to one under merge_policy=EXACT_FORMAL_SEMANTIC_SIGNATURE. u_state then calls project_state(world, out). project_state immediately invokes _validate_state(state, world), whose generic external-state invariant rejects any state with fewer than two branches. Therefore a semantically valid exact merge creates an internal one-branch post-merge state that the next stage rejects before projection.
evidence_chain: test constructs two branches with identical v, K, T and predictions and declares EXACT_FORMAL_SEMANTIC_SIGNATURE merge
_semantic_signature hashes exactly v, K, T and predictions, so the two branches share one declared formal semantic signature
_merge_exact_equivalents deterministically groups by that signature and emits one pivot with merged_from_branch_ids
_validate_state requires len(branches) >= 2 and returns STATE_REQUIRES_AT_LEAST_TWO_BRANCHES for the post-merge state
semantic_interpretation: Exact formal semantic equivalents are duplicate representations of one hypothesis, not unresolved competing hypotheses. Merging them does not violate Hyperposition's requirement to preserve unresolved alternatives. The bug is specifically that the external-input minimum-branch invariant is reused after an internal equivalence collapse where it no longer matches the declared merge semantics.
counterhypothesis: The system may intend every Hyperposition carrier to contain at least two branches even after exact equivalence collapse, in which case the merge operation itself should be forbidden or represented without reducing branch cardinality. That interpretation contradicts the current test contract and the implemented _merge_exact_equivalents behavior, so the source/test pair is internally inconsistent until one invariant is explicitly chosen.
